summary: @ornikar/webpack-config 12.0.8 ships a preinstall dropper that downloads Bun and executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The `preinstall` script `setup.mjs` is heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style `_0xNNNN` identifiers with string-array wrappers). On `npm install`, it constructs a GitHub release URL for the Bun runtime (`https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<archive>.zip`), downloads and extracts the archive, chmods the Bun binary executable, and then invokes it via `execFileSync` to run the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727 KB single-line `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with obfuscator.io-style scrambled identifiers, a large numeric/string constant pool, and a string-shuffling routine — its content is unrelated to webpack configuration. `package.json` declares `"main": "index.js"` but no `index.js` exists in the tarball, so the package has no legitimate library surface; the only auto-executing code is the install-time dropper. Using an alternate runtime (Bun) rather than Node to execute the payload evades JS scanners that only trace Node-resolved code. The behavior pattern (obfuscated preinstall + alternate-runtime execution of a large obfuscated sibling bundle + missing declared main + purpose mismatch with a webpack-config helper) is consistent with a compromised/hijacked release of this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
